parts: All markets pooled: the results file is not split by market, so this view cannot be filtered to one market.

Lags: self-serve orders arrive log-normal from the causing touch (median 31 days, truncated at 91 days); lead-path orders arrive after a quote_request with a tail of up to 365 days. Measured from the FIRST click, the median is longer (43 days self-serve, 50 overall, all orders), because the causing touch is often not the first one.
The repo's weekly dataset truncates the lag at 91 days; the 365-day tail applies to the lead path in this extension only.
GA4's maximum lookback window is 90 days.

parts.01_platform_vs_analytics_gap: ratio > 1.50 = FAIL, ratio > 1.25 = WARN, otherwise OK. SEO and Direct_Other have no platform figure.
parts.02_weekly_volume_anomalies: FLAG when orders are more than 25% below the 8-week median AND more than 3 standard errors below it (standard error approximated as the square root of the median, as for count data). The second condition stops small markets being flagged for ordinary random swings.
parts.03_spend_vs_sessions_sanity: FLAG a row if A) spend > 0 and sessions = 0, B) spend = 0 and sessions > 0, or C) cost per session is more than 4 standard deviations from that market x channel's mean over the full period.
parts.04_revenue_reconciliation: component mismatch = FAIL; revenue per order more than 10% from expected = WARN.

parts.check: weeks where a market's orders fall sharply below its own recent level (possible tracking break or real event).
parts.method: compare each week with the median of the previous 8 weeks, per market, all channels combined.
parts.rule: FLAG when orders are more than 25% below the 8-week median AND more than 3 standard errors below it (standard error approximated as the square root of the median, as for count data). The second condition stops small markets being flagged for ordinary random swings.
parts.note: catches sudden breaks (tag outage, broken checkout), not gradual effects such as the Meta holdout.

parts.rule: FLAG a row if A) spend > 0 and sessions = 0, B) spend = 0 and sessions > 0, or C) cost per session is more than 4 standard deviations from that market x channel's mean over the full period.
